text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERDUTY ALERT — GPU pool 'gpu-p1' failing to scale. Queue length = 8200, active throttles increasing, latency SLOs breached for some routes. Autoscaler attempted multiple launches; several nodes flapped during driver init. Paging oncall.

pagerduty-bot: Triggered incident INC-2026-3175 -> paging @maria, @ajay (primary oncall). Incident runbook: gpu-capacity-exhaustion.

maria: I'm here, grabbing context. Which autoscaler and which fleet?

ajay: oncall. seeing repeated node flaps in gpu-p1 in us-west-2; autoscaler logs show repeated launch failures -> capacity not coming up. Added to channel. :eyes:

tess: dumping kube events and driver logs from the last 30m.

```
# kubectl describe node gpu-node-47
LastHeartbeatTime: Thu Mar 12 15:12:02 UTC 2026
Conditions: Ready=False
Events:
  Warning  NodeNotReady  2m  kubelet  kernel panic -> nvidia driver Xid 184 errors
# dmesg excerpt
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 184, PID=1024, Index=7, Channel=0x00000004
[  123.456790] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

leo: Xid 184 is a device/firmware hang on these AMX-40 cards we've been onboarding. Pattern: driver OOM -> node flaps -> pod restarts -> autoscaler interprets as capacity shortage -> spins up more nodes -> hits same failure -> thrash.

sam: confirma: logs show repeated OOMs from the runtime allocator right after a large batch job. We also see continuous 503s from the hosted API fronting that pool. Customer impact: org-acme and org-beta reported increased 5xx in the last 10m.

maria: important: throttles rising on /v1/generate and embeddings routes. We need immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact while we stabilize driver/runtime.

ajay: proposed immediate actions (taking lead):
1) Pause autoscaling on gpu-p1 (prevent further churn).
2) Manually cordon and drain nodes with repeated Xid/OOMs (gpu-node-47, gpu-node-51).
3) Spin up isolated warm nodes from reserve pool (reserve-s1) that have older driver build (known stable) and pin critical customer traffic there.
4) Enable small-model fallback routing for non-critical routes to reduce load on gpu-p1.

tess: executing commands now.

```
# pause autoscaler
$ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/autoscaler/gpu-p1/pause
{"status":"paused","reason":"investigating node flaps"}
# cordon/drain
$ kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
$ kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

leo: note: draining will trigger a bunch of pending pods due to insufficient spare capacity if we don't bring reserve nodes up first. start reserve nodes concurrently.

ajay: provisioning reserve-s1 +3 nodes (manual allocation).

```
$ cloudctl compute instances create --flavor g4x-large --image redwood-gpu-stable --count 3 --pool reserve-s1
Request accepted -> ops-job-8892
```

sam: routing change: will update model-router to send org-acme critical traffic to reserve-s1 when capacity reports healthy. Non-critical traffic to fallback-small.

maria: coordinating comms: engineering to #support: brief on impacted customers (org-acme, org-beta) and advise reduced throughput & increased latency. I'll draft.

pagerduty-bot: @ajay acknowledged INC-2026-3175. Escalation to SRE lead if unresolved in 20m.

~9m later~

tess: reserve nodes booted, driver version 510.82 (stable). We pinned cuda-runtime 12.1. Quick smoke on small job: PASS.

ajay: moved critical routes for org-acme to reserve-s1. Confirmed 200s for a subset of synthetic requests.

sam: enabled fallback-small routing for generic tenant traffic. Throttling on gpu-p1 reduced immediately. Queue dropped from 8200 -> 1600 observed on the queue dashboard.

leo: collected full kernel logs and will open driver vendor ticket; attaching stack traces and repeated Xid entries. Suspect a regression in new driver 520.x memory alloc path under heavy batching.

maria: update for support: "We've routed critical workloads off the affected pool and enabled smaller-model fallbacks to reduce load. Root cause appears to be a driver/runtime memory failure causing node flaps; engineering is collecting artifacts and engaging the driver vendor. We'll provide timeline update in 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:

ajay: current status: autoscaler paused, drained two flaky nodes (gpu-node-47/51), reserve nodes serving critical traffic, queue decreasing. Continuing to monitor.

pagerduty-bot: Note: incident is still active. Next escalation window in 10m.

maria: I'm handing off to @ajay — I need to step out for 20m. Ajay has lead; reach him via pager if anything urgent.

ajay: taking full lead. Oncall rotation note: I'll keep this channel updated every 5–10m and post final summary when resolved.

~40m later~

sam: dashboard: queue = 420; error rate back to baseline for non-affected routes, org-acme requests 95% success on reserve nodes. No additional node flaps observed on reserve nodes.

leo: uploaded driver logs and vendor case #DV-9876. Vendor acknowledged suspect regression in 520.x and suggested rolling back where possible; recommended kernel parameter tweak as temporary mitigation.

ajay: next steps: repro on staging with 520.x + heavy batching, test vendor kernel tweak, and plan controlled rollback for production if we see repro. Also re-enable autoscaling with stricter health checks and a cool-down window to avoid thrash.

maria: thanks all. I'll update post-incident notes and ping customers with a summary.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3175 — status: Mitigated (traffic shifted, reserve nodes online, autoscaler paused). Final investigator: @ajay.

-- END THREAD --
